```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(glue)
library(knitr)

data_year <- params$data_year
path_to_output <- here("WGRDBESstockCoord/personal/JB/output")

### The folders written by compare_cef_raised_datasets.R and compare_cef_age_allocation.R
dir_raised <- file.path(path_to_output, "cef_raised_CEF-RDBES_vs_CEF-IC", data_year)
dir_age <- file.path(path_to_output, "cef_age_CEF-RDBES_vs_CEF-IC", data_year)

### The plots of both comparisons: named lists, the names are the figure files
plots_raised <- readRDS(file.path(dir_raised, "list_plots.rds"))
plots_age <- readRDS(file.path(dir_age, "list_plots.rds"))

### A plot that may not exist (no stratum differs) is skipped
show_plot <- function(list_plots, name) {
  if (name %in% names(list_plots)) list_plots[[name]]
  else cat("*Nothing to show: no stratum differs.*\n")
}

read_table <- function(dir, name) read_csv(file.path(dir, "tables", paste0(name, ".csv")), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

# What is compared

Two versions of the CEF data of the stock sol.27.8ab, year `r data_year`, are compared:

- **CEF-IC**: the distributions and the catches converted from InterCatch.
- **CEF-RDBES**: the same data as downloaded from the RDBES (`CatchNatEst` and `DistributionNatEst`).

Both go through the same steps, first the discards raising (`sole8ab_cef_*_discards_raising.R`) and then the age
allocation (`sole8ab_cef_*_age_allocation.R`). The plots below come from `compare_cef_raised_datasets.R` and
`compare_cef_age_allocation.R`. In every plot IC is first and RDBES second (orange: IC, grey: RDBES). The countries are
put on the RDBES codes (FR, BE, ...) on both sides. A stratum is a country, catch category, season, area and fleet.

The strata that only one of the two has are shown in the tables (`status`: "only CEF-IC", "only CEF-RDBES"). They mostly
come from differences in the coding of the season (quarter or year), the area (one area or several) and the fleet.

# Discards raising

The catch after the discards raising (`df_stock_overview_L_D_raised`): landings, discards and BMS landings in kg for each
stratum.

## Totals

```{r}
#| label: table-raised-category
read_table(dir_raised, "category") |>
  mutate(across(c(Catchkg_rdbes, Catchkg_ic, difference), \(x) round(x))) |>
  select(catchCategory, strata, strata_differ, CEF_IC = Catchkg_ic, CEF_RDBES = Catchkg_rdbes, difference, ratio) |>
  kable(digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
        caption = "Catch (kg) by catch category. difference = IC minus RDBES, ratio = IC / RDBES.")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-raised-totals
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| fig-cap: "Catch by catch category."
show_plot(plots_raised, "01_totals")
```

## Stratum by stratum

```{r}
#| label: fig-raised-by-stratum
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-cap: "Catch of each stratum in IC against RDBES. On the dashed line the two agree."
show_plot(plots_raised, "02_by_stratum")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-raised-largest
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "The 20 strata whose catch differs most, IC minus RDBES."
show_plot(plots_raised, "03_strata_that_differ_most")
```

# Age allocation

The numbers and mean weights at age after the age allocation (`df_canum_all_age`): the age distribution of a stratum is
either imported from the data (with the SOP correction) or allocated from the strata that have one, with the most
specific rule first (country, quarter and gear, then ...). Ages from 8 are the plus group.

## Totals

```{r}
#| label: table-age-total
read_table(dir_age, "total") |>
  select(catchCategory, strata, strata_differ, numbers_ic, numbers_rdbes, numbers_ratio, sop_kg_ic, sop_kg_rdbes, sop_ratio) |>
  kable(digits = 3, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
        caption = "Numbers (fish) and sum of numbers x mean weights (kg) by catch category. ratio = IC / RDBES.")
```

## At age

```{r}
#| label: fig-age-numbers
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Numbers at age, landings and discards."
show_plot(plots_age, "01_numbers_at_age")
```

```{r}

#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Mean weight at age, landings and discards."
```
